problem_text: I have an existing Fabric workspace called ws_RTI_BicycleRentals built around Real-Time Intelligence. It contains an Eventhouse (eh_RTI_BicycleRentals) with one KQL database, an Eventstream (es_RTI_BicycleRentals), an Activator (activator_BicycleRentals), an Anomaly Detection item (anomalies_BicycleRentals), a Real-Time Dashboard (dashboard_BicycleRentals), a Map (map_RTI_BicycleRentals), a Lakehouse (lh_RTI_BicycleRentals), a Semantic Model (sm_RTI_BicycleRentals), and a Report (rpt_RTI_BicycleRentals). The workspace is connected to a GitHub repo on the dev-fabric-sync branch, last synced 7/27/2026. The Fabric capacity is PAYG in North Europe. I want you to read what is already deployed, document the current RTI architecture, identify any gaps, and describe what a complete end-to-end deployment would look like. Do not create any new items.

candidate_intents.summary: User wants data scientists / ML practitioners to access and explore organizational data
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User is describing a gap between data availability and analytical/ML use of that data. Triggers Python/ML runtime + curated historical store.

candidate_intents.summary: User wants natural-language or AI-assisted querying of data
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User wants non-technical users (analysts, executives) to interrogate data without writing SQL or KQL. Triggers DataAgent with governed semantic context.

candidate_intents.summary: User has long historical record and wants to derive value from it
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User has a large historical corpus that needs cheap durable storage AND a structure suitable for analytical workloads (medallion bronze/silver/gold).

candidate_intents.summary: User has manual/paper-based field intake and wants to digitize it
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User has humans in the field capturing data manually. Triggers a low-code mobile/form-friendly ingest path (Power Apps + CopyJob/DataPipeline into lakehouse bronze).

candidate_intents.summary: User needs sub-minute (often sub-second) reaction to incoming signals
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User cannot tolerate batch latency. Triggers Eventstream (ingest) + Eventhouse (low-latency store) + KQL Dashboard or Real-Time Dashboard (serve).

candidate_intents.summary: User wants automated alerts or actions when thresholds are crossed
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User needs reactive automation. Triggers Activator/Reflex on top of the streaming or analytical layer.

candidate_intents.summary: User explicitly prefers low-code or SQL-first tooling for ingestion/transforms
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User wants to keep existing SQL/BI team productive without forcing them into PySpark. Bias ingestion toward CopyJob/DataPipeline/Dataflow Gen2.

candidate_intents.summary: User wants code-first Python/Spark for ML/AI workloads even if other workloads are low-code
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User has or wants ML practitioners working in code. Triggers Notebook (Python/PySpark) bound to Lakehouse + optional MLModel/MLExperiment.

candidate_intents.summary: User wants governed semantic model for analyst self-service reporting
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User wants governed BI consumption. Triggers SemanticModel + Report layered on Lakehouse SQL endpoint or Warehouse.

candidate_intents.summary: User must handle regulated, sensitive, or governed data
candidate_intents.llm_hint: User has regulatory obligations. Triggers Variable Library for secrets + workspace-level governance + sensitivity labels.

instructions: Read the problem_text. For each intent_id under candidates_to_consider, decide whether the problem genuinely expresses that intent — even when the user does not use exact keywords. Return only intents with confidence 'high' or 'medium'. Be conservative: if the signal is weak, omit the intent. Do NOT invent new intent_ids. Cite a short quote from the problem_text in 'rationale' for every returned intent.
